summary: A0020 (PROPHET, no target task) is safe and coherent; every claim in its record that I could test reproduced exactly. Scope: cb7d6a4 is the single child of the base commit and touches five paths only - docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md (M), todo/README.md (M), todo/amendments/A0020/{request.json,prophet-001.json,impacts.json} (A, the controller/Prophet amendment-record shape A0018/A0019 already use). No path under tools/workflow/, .claude/, todo/schemas/, .github/, src/, tests/, no todo/phases/** change, no deletion (git diff --diff-filter=D empty), no dependency-manifest change. Frozen state: todo/config.yaml is byte-identical to base, so no pre-existing task's status, attempt, commits, evidence, review pointer, dependency, phase or contract path moved, and both revisions are unchanged (the Owner direction forbade editing that file). Existing contracts byte-identical: no contract file appears in the diff; the 83 configured contract paths equal the 83 files on disk, no orphans. No gate weakened: the same three checks pass on base and candidate (check_citations, check_imports, check_acceptance all 'no findings'; python -m tools.workflow validate OK; full pytest 2316 passed, 6 skipped with tests/test_abi_artifacts.py deselected, and 2316-34=2282 exactly matches the record's quoted 2282+6 when that whole file is excluded). No Must-not clause, acceptance criterion, test assertion or suppression entry was removed or added; nothing was hidden behind docs/implement/ci/suppressions.toml, which is untouched. Mechanism verified rather than trusted: simulating the retirement in memory (superseded_by=T105/T106/T107/T108 on the four predecessors, config copy in /tmp, no repo write) and running the repository's own resolver reproduces the archived FAIL exactly - base rows give 8 architecture-section22 findings at lines 119/120/122/123 and 155-158 - while the candidate rows give 0 findings both with and without the retirement recorded; the cited clauses resolve to what the record says (tools/check_citations/resolvers.py:468-485 superseded-by requirement, :506-514 token expansion, todo/WORKFLOW.md:222-225 plan-structure revision, :144-155 SUPERSEDE's single-field limit, tools/workflow/core.py:1704-1706 SUPERSEDE path limit, layer_map.py:69/:140, check_imports/architecture.py:102 _TASK.fullmatch, T005.md:32-33, T006.md:35-38, ci.yml:54-60). Staleness: I searched every live document for what the changed documents touch and found no sentence left contradicting the edit - the four successor rows lost '(successor to T06x)' and no other live file (grep 'successor to', '(successor', 'predecessor delivery') quoted that text; P06/README.md ('designated current successor after retirement'), TRACEABILITY.md:75-76, ADR-003:73-74, ADR-008:86-89, ADR-006:70, THREAT_MODEL:369-463, AUTHORING_GUIDE:3-8 and todo/README.md:326 all already use the 'after retirement / designated successor' framing this annotation matches; todo/README.md lost no line (355 lines before and after), so section-based citations there stay valid. affected_existing_tasks=[] tested, not accepted: the four predecessor contracts (T063/T064/T066/T067) and the four successor contracts (T105-T108) contain no ARCHITECTURE or section-2.2 reference at all, so the annotation cannot falsify them; the contracts that do cite section 2.2 (T000, T005, T006, T007, T012, T068, T084) cite layers and module ownership that the diff leaves byte-identical. resolved_task_impacts=[] is right: recomputing the register with the controller's own rule leaves exactly four open impacts (A0013:T063/T064/T066/T067:legacy, all about registry identity in the Deliverables, not about this table) and this change neither repairs nor worsens them, nor raises any new one. Implementation/data/operations: docs-only; no src/, tests/, CLI, Web, background, risk, execution or signer path reads ARCHITECTURE.md at runtime (only the two checkers do), no persisted artifact, schema, manifest or migration changes; the one real operational fact - the annotation must land before the retirement can be re-issued, because SUPERSEDE may change only superseded_by and cannot repair this table - is identified and is true. Consumer closure: config is unchanged, so dependency closures and the set of PLANNED dependents are unchanged, and the only PLANNED dependents of T063/T064/T066/T067 are their four successors T105-T108 (the ordinary consumers were re-pointed by A0014). Provenance/secrets: no credential, URL, keystore path or env value in any changed file; the record's mutable facts carry sources plus the 2026-09-20 retrieval date, and the one external artifact it names - branch amendment/a0020-attempt-001-failed, tip 403c6bdfc4acc0a4cf4463ce6fcb8c570e2de602 - exists, is not an ancestor of main, and its archived review-001.json is a FAIL whose 8 findings are the same 8 I reproduced. Two imprecisions I verified and cleared, neither affecting any gate: (1) ARCHITECTURE.md:182 says 'no section-2.2 row is read as a reference to a task under retirement'; the four predecessor rows are themselves read as references to T063/T064/T066/T067 and pass only because they name the successor, so the sentence is exact for the successor rows and for the gate outcome but overbroad if read absolutely - I confirmed rows 119/120/122/123 are the only rows carrying those tokens; (2) prophet-001.json's rationale says todo/config.yaml 'still has no superseded_by' when it in fact records three (T022/T023/T038); the claim is true for the four predecessors, which is what the wording choice depends on, and it is what makes the chosen 'superseded by T10x' form (without 'retired;') the accurate one for an unrecorded retirement. One disclosed residual, narrower than the record describes: annotating the predecessor rows makes tools/check_imports/architecture.py skip those rows, but I parsed both trees and the set of modules under the section-2.2/layer-map agreement check is identical before and after (52 rows each; robinhood_lp.reports.*, robinhood_lp.robustness and robinhood_lp.experiments simply move from rows 119/120/122 to rows 155/156/157 with the same layer strings), so no module lost verification and no disagreement is masked; the T022/T023/T038 rows have carried the same annotation form since A0008.
